questions.question:
A \(100\text-\)turn closely wound circular coil of radius \(5~\text{cm}\) has a magnetic field of \(3.14 \times 10^{-3}~\text{T}\) at its centre. The current flowing through the coil, and the magnitude of the magnetic moment of this coil are, respectively:
(take \(\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}~\text{T-m/A}\))
1. \(2.5~\text{A}, 2~\text{A-m}^2\)
2. \(2.5~\text{A}, 20~\text{A-m}^2\)
3. \(2~\text{A},4~\text{A-m}^2\)
4. \(2~\text{A}, 10~\text{A-m}^2\)
questions.explanation:
Hint: \(m=NIA\)

Step 1: Find the current flowing through the coil.
For a circular coil, the magnetic field at the centre is given by;
\(B = \dfrac{\mu_0N I}{2R}\)
\(\Rightarrow I = \dfrac{2BR}{\mu_0 N}\)
\(\Rightarrow I = \dfrac{2\times 3.14\times 10^{-3}\times 5\times 10^{-2}}{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 100}= 2.5~\text{A}\)

Step 2: Find the magnitude of the magnetic moment of this coil.
The magnetic moment of the coil is given by;
\(m=NIA\)
\(\Rightarrow m=100 \times 2.5 \times 3.14 \times 25 \times 10^{-4}\)
\(\Rightarrow m=196\times 10^{-2}= 1.96 ~\text{A m}^2\)
\(\Rightarrow m\approx 2 ~\text{A m}^2\)
Hence, option (1) is the correct answer.

The current \(I\) in the circuit shown below is:
(All diodes are ideal and identical.)

1. \(\dfrac{5}{3}~\text{A}\)

2. \(\dfrac{15}{2} ~\text{A}\)

3. \(\dfrac{1}{3} ~\text{A}\)

4. \(\dfrac{5}{9} ~\text{A}\)
questions.explanation:
Hint: Check diode direction: only forward-biased branches conduct.

Step: The current flowing through the coil.
When the \(\mathrm{p\text-}\)side of the diode is connected to positive terminal of the battery and   \(\mathrm{n\text-}\)side of the diode is connected to negative terminal of the battery then the diode is forward biased and current will flow through diode.
When the \(\mathrm{n\text-}\)side of the diode is connected to positive terminal of the battery and \(\mathrm{p\text-}\)side of the diode is connected to negative terminal of the battery then the diode is reverse biased so, no current will flow through the diode. 
So, the current will flow through resistor \(4~\Omega~\text{and}~2~\Omega\). The resistor \(4~\Omega~\text{and}~2~\Omega\) are connected in parallel.
The equivalent resistance of the circuit is given by;
\(R_{eq} = \dfrac{4\times 2}{4+2} = \dfrac{4}{3}~\Omega\)
The current flowing through the coil is given by;
\(I = \dfrac{10}{\dfrac{4}{3}}= \dfrac{30}{4} \)
\(\Rightarrow I =\dfrac{15}{2}~\text{A}\)
Hence, option (2) is the correct answer.

In vernier callipers, \(20\) VSD coincides with \(16\) MSD (each division of length \(1\) mm). The least count of the vernier callipers is:
1. \(0.01\) cm
2. \(0.1\) cm
3. \(0.02\) cm
4. \(0.2\) cm
questions.explanation:
Hint: LC\(=1\) MSD\(-1\) VSD

Step: Find the least count of the vernier callipers.
The least count of the vernier calliper is given by;
\(LC = 1MSD -1VSD\)
Given in the question;
\(20~VSD= 16~MSD\)
\(\Rightarrow 1~VSD = \dfrac{16}{20}~MSD\)
\(\Rightarrow LC = 1MSD -\dfrac{4}{5}MSD = \dfrac{1}{5}MSD\)
\(\Rightarrow LC = 0.2~\text{mm}~~~~~~~~~[1MSD = 1~\text{mm}]\)
\(\Rightarrow LC = 0.02~\text{cm}\)

questions.question:
A uniform metallic wire having resistance \(4~\Omega\) is bent to form a square loop \((ABCD)\) (see figure). A resistance of \(2~\Omega\) is connected between points \(B\) and \(D\) and a battery of \(2~\text{V}\) is connected across points \(A\) and \(C\) as shown in the figure. Now the value of the current \((I)\) is:
          
1. \(2~\text{A}\)
2. \(4~\text{A}\)
3. \(8~\text{A}\)
4. \(4.5~\text{A}\)
questions.explanation:
Hint: Identify the Wheatstone bridge.

Step: Find the value of the current \(I\).
The total resistance of the uniform square wire is \(4~\Omega\). Since the square has four equal sides, so \(R_{AB}= R_{BC}= R_{CD}= R_{DA} = 1~\Omega\)
A \(2~\Omega\) resistor is connected across diagonal \(BD\), and a \(2~\text{V}\) battery is connected across opposite corners \(A\) and \(C\). As arrangement is perfectly balanced Wheatstone Bridge so current will flow about \(BD\).
The equivalent resistance between points  \(A\) and \(C\)  is given by;
\(R_{eq} = (1+1)||(1+1)=\dfrac{(2\times 2)}{2+2}= 1~\Omega\)
The current through the circuit is given by;
\(I = \dfrac{V}{R_{eq}} = \dfrac{2}{1} = 2~\text{A}\)
Hence, option (1) is the correct answer.

An unknown nucleus has a nuclear density of \(2.29 \times 10^{17} ~\text{kg/m}^3\) and mass of \(19.926 \times 10^{-27} \text{ kg}\). Its mass number \(A\) is approximately:
(take \(R_0 = 1.2 \times 10^{-15} \text{ m}\), \(4\pi = 12.56\))
1. \(12\)
2. \(19\)
3. \(20\)
4. \(16\)
questions.explanation:
Hint: \(R = R_0 A^{1/3}\)

Step: Find the mass number \(A\).
The nuclear density of the nucleus is given by;
\(\rho = \dfrac{m}{V}= \dfrac{m}{\dfrac{4\pi}{3}R^3_0A}\)
\(\Rightarrow A= \dfrac{3m}{{4\pi}R^3_0\rho}\)
\(\Rightarrow A= \dfrac{3\times 19.926 \times 10^{-27}}{{4\pi}\times 1.728\times 10^{-45}\times 2.29 \times 10^{17}}\)
\(\Rightarrow A=12\)
Hence, option (1) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
A rectangular wire loop of sides \(8\) cm and \(3\) cm with a small cut is moving out of a region of uniform magnetic field of magnitude \(0.3\) T directed normal to the plane of the loop. The emf developed across the cut, if the velocity of the loop is \(2\) cm-s-1, in a direction normal to the shorter side of the loop, will be:
1. \(1.8\times 10^{-4}\) volts
2. \(1.2\times 10^{-4}\) volts
3. \(1.3\times 10^{-4}\) volts
4. \(4.8\times 10^{-4}\) volts
questions.explanation:
Hint: \(E=Blv\)

Step: Find the induced emf across the loop.
As the loop moves out of the magnetic field, the induced emf is given by the rate of change of magnetic flux:
\(\varepsilon = B \dfrac{dA}{dt}= Blv\)
\(\Rightarrow \varepsilon = 0.3 \times 0.03\times 2\times 10^{-2}= 1.8 \times 10^{-4}~\text{Volts}\)
Therefore, the induced emf is \(1.8\times 10^{-4}\) V.
Hence, option (1) is the correct answer.

1. \(0.01~\Omega\)
2. \(0.10~\Omega\)
3. \(0.001~\Omega\)
4. \(1.0~\Omega\)
questions.explanation:
Hint: \(S = \dfrac{I_g G}{I_s}\)

Step: Find the value of shunt resistance.
For conversion into an ammeter, a shunt \(S\) is connected in parallel i.e., \(S (I-I_g)= I_g G\)
\(\Rightarrow S = \dfrac{I_g G}{I-I_g}\)
\(\Rightarrow S = \dfrac{10^{-3}\times 100}{10}= 10^{-2}~\Omega\)
\(\Rightarrow S = 0.01~\Omega\)
Hence, option (1) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In Young's double-slit experiment, using monochromatic light of wavelength \(\lambda,\) the intensity of light at a point on the screen where the path difference is \(\lambda,\) is \(K\) units. The intensity of light at a point where the path difference is \(\dfrac{\lambda}{3}\) will be:
1. \(\dfrac{K}{4}\)
2. \(K\)
3. \(\dfrac{K}{2}\)
4. \(2K\)
questions.explanation:
Hint: \(I = I_{\max} \cos^2\left(\dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)\)

Step: Find the intensity of light at a point where the path difference is \(\dfrac{\lambda}{3}\).
When the path difference is \(\Delta = \lambda\) then the phase difference is \(\pi\).
The intensity of the light is given by;
\(I = K = I_{max}\)
If the path difference is \(\Delta = \dfrac{\lambda}{3}\)
The phase difference is given by;
\(\phi = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda}\times \dfrac{\lambda}{3}= \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\)
The intensity of light at a point is given by;
\(I = I_{max}\cos^2\dfrac{\phi}{2}\)
\(\Rightarrow I = I_{max}\cos^2\dfrac{\dfrac{2\pi}{3}}{2} = I_{max}\cos^2\dfrac{{\pi}}{3}\)
\(\Rightarrow I = \dfrac{K}{4}\)
Hence, option (1) is the correct answer.

The magnitude and direction of the acceleration produced in a body of mass \(5\) kg when two mutually perpendicular forces \(8\) N and \(6\) N act on it are, respectively:
1. \(2 ~\text{ms}^{-2} ; \tan ^{-1}(3 / 4)~\text { with}~ 6~ \text{N force}\)
2. \(2 ~\text{ms}^{-2} ; \mathrm{tan}^{-1}(4 / 3)\text { with}~ 8 ~\text{N force} \)
3. \(2 ~\text{ms}^{-2} ; \tan ^{-1}(3 / 4)\text { with} ~8 ~\text{N force} \)
4. \(20~ \text{ms}^{-2}; \tan ^{-1}(4 / 3)\text { with}~ 8 ~\text{N force}\)
questions.explanation:
Hint: \(F_{\mathrm{net}}=ma\)

Step: Find the magnitude and direction of the acceleration produced in a body.
The resultant of the force is given by;
\(R = \sqrt{8^2+ 6^2}= 10~\text{N}\)
The acceleration produced in the body is given by;
\(a = \dfrac{F}{m}= \dfrac{10}{5} = 2~\text{m/s}^2\)
Let the \(8~\text{N}\) force be the reference axis. The direction of the force is given by;
\(\tan\theta = \dfrac{3}{4}\) 
\(\Rightarrow \theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)\)
Therefore, the magnitude and direction of the acceleration produced in a body is \(2 ~\text{ms}^{-2} ; \tan ^{-1}(3 / 4)\text { with} ~8 ~\text{N force} \).
Hence, option (3) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Five capacitors of capacitances;
\(C_1=C_2=C_3=C_4 = 10~\mu\text{F}\) and \(C_5 = 2.5~\mu\text{F}\) are connected as shown, along with a battery of \(50\) V.

The equivalent capacitance and the charges on each capacitor, respectively, are:
1. \(5~\mu\text{F}, 125~\mu\text{C}\) on all capacitors
2. \(5~\mu\text{F}, 250~\mu\text{C}\) on all capacitors
3. \(4~\mu\text{F}, 250~\mu\text{C}\) on \(C_1\) to \(C_4\) and \(125~\mu\text{C}\) on \(C_5\)
4. \(5~\mu\text{F}, 125~\mu\text{C}\) on  \(C_1\) to \(C_4\) and \(25~\mu\text{C}\) on \(C_5\)
questions.explanation:
Hint: \(Q=CV\)

Step: Find the equivalent capacitance and charge on the capacitor. 
The capacitors \(C_1,C_2,C_3, C_4 \) are connected in series and the equivalent capacitance of the \(C_1,C_2,C_3, C_4 \) is given by;
\(\dfrac{C}{n} \)
The equivalent capacitance of \(C_1,C_2,C_3, C_4 \) is given by;
\(C_{1,2,3,4} = \dfrac{10}{4} = 2.5~\mu\text{F}\)
Now, the capacitor \(2.5~\mu\text{F}\) and \(C_5 = 2.5~\mu\text{F}\) are connected in parallel and the equivalent capacitance of the circuit is given by;
\(C_{eq} = 2.5 + 2.5 = 5~\mu\text{F}\)
The charge flowing through the circuit is given by;
\(Q= C_{eq} V = 5 \times 50 = 250~\mu\text{C}\)
The charge on the capacitors \(C_1,C_2,C_3, C_4 \) is given by;
\(Q_{1,2,3,4} = \dfrac{2.5\times 250}{5} = 125~\mu\text{C}\)
Similarly, the charge on the capacitor \(C_5\) is given by;
\(Q_{5} = \dfrac{2.5\times 250}{5} = 125~\mu\text{C}\)
Therefore, the equivalent capacitance and the charges on each capacitor, respectively are \(5~\mu\text{F}, 125~\mu\text{C}\) on each capacitor. 
Hence, option (1) is the correct answer.

In a metre bridge experiment (see figure), the positions of the cell, \(E,\) and galvanometer, \(G,\) are interchanged. We shall observe in the galvanometer:
1. Only the right-sided deflection.
2. Only the left-sided deflection.

4. Both right-sided and left-sided deflection and, at balance point, no deflection.
questions.explanation:
Hint: Swapping battery and galvanometer positions does not affect the balance condition.

Explanation: In a metre bridge (Wheatstone bridge), the balance condition depends only on the ratio of resistances in the two arms. If the positions of the cell \(E\) and galvanometer \(G\) are interchanged, the bridge still works on the same principle because of the reciprocity property of Wheatstone bridge circuits. 
So, when the jockey is on one side of the balance point then deflection in one direction,
when it is on the other side then deflection in the opposite direction, at the balance point then no deflection.
Hence, option (4) is the correct answer.

Match List-I with List-II
List-I List-II
A. Young's Modulus I. \(-\dfrac{\Delta d}{\Delta L} \left( \dfrac{L}{d} \right)\)
B. Compressibility II. \(\dfrac{FL}{A(\Delta L)}\)
C. Bulk Modulus III. \(-\dfrac{1}{\Delta P} \left( \dfrac{\Delta V}{V} \right)\)
D. Poisson's Ratio IV. \(-P \left( \dfrac{V}{\Delta V} \right)\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
1. \(\mathrm{A\text-I, B\text{-}IV, C\text-III, D\text{-}II}\)
2. \(\mathrm{A\text-IV, B\text{-}I, C\text-II, D\text{-}III}\)
3. \(\mathrm{A\text-III, B\text{-}II, C\text-I, D\text{-}IV}\)
4. \(\mathrm{A\text-II, B\text{-}III, C\text-IV, D\text{-}I}\)
questions.explanation:
Hint: Compressibility\(=\dfrac{1}{\text{Bulk Modulus}}\)

Step: Find the correct match. 
The Young's modulus of the material is given by;
\(Y = \dfrac{FL}{A\Delta L}\)
The Compressibility of the material is given by;
\(\text{Compressibility} = \dfrac{1}{\text{Bulk modulus}} =- \dfrac{1}{P}\left(\dfrac{V}{\Delta V}\right)\)
The bulk modulus of the material is given by;
\(B = -P\left(\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}\right)\)
The Poisson's ratio of the material is given by;
\(\sigma = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{\Delta d}{d}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{\Delta L}{L}\right)} = \dfrac{\Delta d}{\Delta L}\left(\dfrac{L}{d}\right)\)
Therefore, the correct match is \(\mathrm{A\text-II, B\text{-}III, C\text-IV, D\text{-}I}\).
Hence, option (4) is the correct answer.

(consider the density of water\(=1000 ~\text{kg m}^{-3},\) \(1 ~\text{atm}=1\times 10^{5} ~\text{Pa}\) and gravitational acceleration \(g=10~\text{m/s}^2\))
1. \(9900~\text{m}\)
2. \(99~\text{m}\)
3. \(9000~\text{m}\)
4. \(990~\text{m}\)
questions.explanation:
Hint: \(\Delta P=\rho gh\)

Step: Find the maximum depth below which a submarine can go.
At the surface, pressure is \(1~\text{atm}\). So pressure due to water alone can be \(100-1 =99~\text{atm}= 99\times 10^{5}~\text{Pa}\). 
The difference in the pressure is given by;
\(\Delta P=\rho gh\)
\(\Rightarrow 99\times 10^{5}=1000 \times 10h\)
\(\Rightarrow h = 990~\text{m}\)
Hence, option (4) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct?
\(\mathrm{A.}\) Inside a conductor, the electrostatic field is zero.
\(\mathrm{B.}\) The electric field at the surface of a charged conductor does not depend on its surface charge density.
\(\mathrm{C.}\) The interior of a charged conductor can have no excess charge in the static situation.
\(\mathrm{D.}\) At the surface of a charged conductor, the electrostatic field must be normal to the surface at every point.
\(\mathrm{E.}\) The electrostatic potential is zero everywhere inside a charged conductor.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
1. \(\mathrm{C,D~\text{and}~E}~\text{only}\)
2. \(\mathrm{A,B~\text{and}~D}~\text{only}\)
3. \(\mathrm{A,C~\text{and}~D}~\text{only}\)
4. \(\mathrm{A,C~\text{and}~E}~\text{only}\)
questions.explanation:
Hint: Inside a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium: electric field is zero.

Step: Analyse each statement one by one.
Inside a conductor, the electrostatic field is zero. This statement is true. In electrostatic equilibrium, free charges rearrange so that the electric field inside the conductor becomes zero.
The electric field at the surface of a charged conductor does not depend on its surface charge density. This statement is true. The surface electric field is related to surface charge density by; \(E = \dfrac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}\) so electric field depend upon surface charge density.
The interior of a charged conductor can have no excess charge in the static situation. This statement is true, as excess charge resides only on the outer surface of a conductor.
At the surface of a charged conductor, the electrostatic field must be normal to the surface at every point. This statement is also correct because any tangential component would move charges, violating electrostatic equilibrium.
The electrostatic potential is zero everywhere inside a charged conductor. This statement is incorrect. The potential is constant, not necessarily zero.
Therefore, the correct statements are \(\mathrm{A, C~\text{and}~D}\) only.
Hence, option (3) is the correct answer.

When \(1 \text{ dm}^3\) of \(\text{CO}_2\) gas is passed over hot coke, the volume of gaseous mixture after complete reaction at STP becomes \(1.4 \text{ dm}^3\). The composition of the gaseous mixture at STP is :
1.  \(0.6 \text{ dm}^3\) of \(\text{CO},\) \(0.8 \text{ dm}^3\) of \(\text{CO}_2\)
2.  \(0.8 \text{ dm}^3\) of \(\text{CO},\) \(0.8 \text{ dm}^3\) of \(\text{CO}_2\)
3.  \(0.8 \text{ dm}^3\) of \(\text{CO},\) \(0.6 \text{ dm}^3\) of \(\text{CO}_2\)
4. \(0.6 \text{ dm}^3\) of \(\text{CO},\) \(0.4 \text{ dm}^3\) of \(\text{CO}_2\)
questions.explanation:
Hint: CO₂ + C → 2CO
 
 

The reaction between CO₂ (carbon dioxide) and hot coke (mostly carbon) is:

CO2(g)+C(s)→2CO(g)

This means that 1 mole of CO₂ reacts with 1 mole of carbon to produce 2 moles of CO.

Volume Relationship:

According to Avogadro's law, at STP, the volume of a gas is directly proportional to the number of moles.

  • Initial volume of CO₂ = 1 dm³.
  • During the reaction, 1 dm³ of CO₂ produces 2 dm³ of CO.

Thus, after the reaction, the total volume of the mixture will be:

  • CO₂ is consumed (it decreases in volume).
  • CO is produced (it increases in volume).

CO₂ + C → 2CO

Initial volume of CO₂ = 1 dm³

Let x dm³ of CO₂ react with coke.

After reaction:

  • CO₂ consumed = x dm³
  • CO formed = 2x dm³
  • Remaining CO₂ = (1 − x) dm³

Final volume of gaseous mixture:

2x + (1 − x) = 1 + x

Given final volume = 1.4 dm³

So,

1 + x = 1.4
x = 0.4 dm³

Therefore:

  • CO formed = 2 × 0.4 = 0.8 dm³
  • CO₂ left = 1 − 0.4 = 0.6 dm³

✅ Correct answer: Option 3 — 0.8 dm³ of CO and 0.6 dm³ of CO₂.

Identify the correct statement about ClF3 from the following options :
1. It has a trigonal pyramidal geometry with two lone pairs on Cl atom
2. It has T-shaped geometry with two lone pairs on Cl atom
3. It has a trigonal planar geometry with two lone pairs on Cl atom
4. It has T-shaped geometry with three lone pairs on Cl atom
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Analysis of ClF₃ (Chlorine Trifluoride):

  1. Electron Configuration of Chlorine:
    • Chlorine is in Group 17 (halogens), meaning it has 7 valence electrons.
    • When it forms a compound like ClF₃, it bonds with three fluorine (F) atoms. Fluorine, being highly electronegative, forms bonds with chlorine by using its lone pairs, leaving chlorine with lone pairs of its own.
  2. Lewis Structure of ClF₃:
    • Chlorine (Cl) will be the central atom, and three fluorine (F) atoms will be bonded to it.
    • Chlorine has 7 valence electrons, and each fluorine contributes 1 electron. This gives us 3 bonding pairs of electrons from fluorine.
    • Since chlorine has 7 valence electrons and 3 are involved in bonding with fluorine atoms, 4 electrons remain as lone pairs on the chlorine atom.
  3. Geometry of ClF₃:
    • The molecule has 3 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs of electrons on the chlorine atom.
    • According to the VSEPR theory (Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion theory), with 3 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs, the electron pair geometry is trigonal bipyramidal.
    • However, the presence of 2 lone pairs on the chlorine atom will distort the geometry. The lone pairs will occupy the equatorial positions of the trigonal bipyramidal arrangement to minimize repulsion, leaving the fluorine atoms in the axial positions.
    • This results in a T-shaped geometry.

Answer Choices:

  • Option 1: It has a trigonal pyramidal geometry with two lone pairs on the Cl atom.
    • Incorrect. The geometry is not trigonal pyramidal; it is T-shaped due to the arrangement of lone pairs and bonding pairs.
  • Option 2: It has T-shaped geometry with two lone pairs on the Cl atom.
    • Correct. The geometry of ClF₃ is T-shaped, and there are 2 lone pairs on the chlorine atom, which occupy the equatorial positions in the trigonal bipyramidal arrangement.
  • Option 3: It has a trigonal planar geometry with two lone pairs on the Cl atom.
    • Incorrect. The geometry is not trigonal planar; it is T-shaped.
  • Option 4: It has T-shaped geometry with three lone pairs on the Cl atom.
    • Incorrect. There are only 2 lone pairs on the chlorine atom, not 3.

questions.question:
The functional group that can be identified through phthalein dye test is:
1. Phenolic
2. Alcohol
3. Aldehyde
4. Carboxylic acid
questions.explanation:
The phthalein dye test is commonly used to identify the presence of certain functional groups in organic compounds. This test uses phthalein dyes, which are specific for certain groups, especially phenolic compounds.

Phthalein Dye Test:

  • Phenolphthalein and other phthalein dyes are often used in acid-base titrations. They undergo color changes depending on the pH of the solution.
  • The phthalein dye test is specifically used to detect phenolic compounds. In the test:
    • If a phenolic compound is present, the phthalein dye will turn a pink color in an alkaline medium. This is because the hydroxyl group (-OH) in phenolic compounds reacts with the dye, causing the color change.

Explanation of the Options:

  1. Phenolic: Correct. Phthalein dye (especially phenolphthalein) is commonly used to identify phenolic compounds. The color change in the test indicates the presence of a phenolic hydroxyl group (-OH).
  2. Alcohol: Incorrect. While alcohols also contain hydroxyl groups, phthalein dye is more specific for phenols, not alcohols. Alcohols typically do not cause the same color change with phthalein dyes.
  3. Aldehyde: Incorrect. The phthalein dye test is not used to identify aldehydes. Aldehydes are typically detected using other reagents, like Tollens' reagent or Fehling's reagent.
  4. Carboxylic acid: Incorrect. Carboxylic acids can be detected using other tests (e.g., reacting with sodium bicarbonate to release CO₂), but phthalein dyes are not specific for carboxylic acids.

questions.question:
A mixture of chloroform and acetone forms a solution with negative deviation from Raoult's law due to :
1. formation of hydrogen bonding between acetone and chloroform.
2. increase in the escaping tendency of molecules of each component.
3. stronger intermolecular forces between chloroform molecules than those between chloroform and acetone molecules.
4. repulsive forces.
questions.explanation:
A solution shows a negative deviation from Raoult’s law when the observed vapor pressure is lower than the ideal vapor pressure. This happens when the intermolecular forces between the components of the solution are stronger than the forces between the individual molecules of each component.

Why Chloroform and Acetone Show Negative Deviation:

When chloroform (CHCl₃) and acetone (C₃H₆O) are mixed, they exhibit stronger intermolecular interactions than what would be expected based on the individual components. This results in a lower vapor pressure than predicted, because the solution forms strong hydrogen bonds between the acetone (which has a hydrogen atom attached to oxygen) and chloroform (which has a hydrogen attached to chlorine).

Analysis of the Options:

  1. Formation of hydrogen bonding between acetone and chloroform:
    • Correct. Acetone and chloroform form hydrogen bonds between the oxygen of acetone and the hydrogen of chloroform, which leads to stronger intermolecular forces and a lower vapor pressure, causing negative deviation from Raoult’s law.
  2. Increase in the escaping tendency of molecules of each component:
    • Incorrect. In a negative deviation, the escaping tendency of molecules is lower, not higher, because the molecules are more strongly attracted to each other due to the formation of hydrogen bonds.
  3. Stronger intermolecular forces between chloroform molecules than those between chloroform and acetone molecules:
    • Incorrect. The negative deviation occurs because of stronger interactions between acetone and chloroform (due to hydrogen bonding), not because of stronger forces between chloroform molecules themselves.
  4. Repulsive forces:
    • Incorrect. Repulsive forces would lead to a positive deviation from Raoult's law, where the vapor pressure would be higher than expected. Negative deviation results from attractive interactions between the molecules.

    • Al (Aluminum) has a larger atomic radius than Mg (Magnesium) because of the difference in their atomic numbers and electron configuration.
    • Mg²⁺ has a smaller ionic radius compared to Al³⁺, as the higher charge on Al³⁺ results in a stronger attraction between the nucleus and electrons, pulling the electrons closer to the nucleus.

• Statement A: True. Restriction endonucleases are commonly referred to as 'molecular scissors' because they cut DNA molecules at specific locations.

• Statement B: True. These enzymes are part of the bacterial defense system. They function to 'restrict' the growth of viruses (bacteriophages) by cutting up their DNA upon entry into the bacterial cell (like E. coli).

• Statement C: False. Restriction enzymes do not always cut at the centre of the palindromic site. The word 'only' makes this statement incorrect.

• Statement D: False. This is the definition of exonucleases. Endonucleases (like restriction endonucleases) cut DNA at specific internal positions, not from the ends. Therefore, statement D is incorrect.

• Statement E: True. Each restriction endonuclease identifies a specific recognition sequence, which is typically a palindromic base-pair sequence.

Since the question asks for statements that are not true, the incorrect statements are C and D.
